The species Pseudorasbora parva and its golden breeding form have not been traded since 2016 due to an EU-wide trade ban.

This is a golden sport (the scientific term for this phenomenon is xanthorism) of the Stone moroko (Pseudorasbora parva). The specimens are bred ones. Available size: 6-8 cm.

The Stone moroko originates from Asia, where it occurs naturally in the northeastern parts (former USSR, China, Japan, etc.). In the 1970s it was introduced to Central Europe along with fish imported for stocking waters for fishing purposes. Since then it has spread rapidly all over the continent.

The Stone moroko is a vigorous and absolutely undemanding species, which explains its great success. It often becomes the only fish species in a biotope after some time. They fit very small garden ponds, rain barrels etc., in which no other fish species would survive. During winter the fish have to be kept in a cool tank in the cellar, as even these hardy fish cannot survive deep-freezing.
Stone morokos tolerate a broad range of temperatures and are absolutely undemanding in respect of water chemistry.
In ponds they feed on mosquito larvae, which makes them quite useful.
They show brood care. The eggs are attached to hard substrate and are guarded by the male until they hatch.
Pseudorasbora: ancient Greek, means "false Rasbora". Rasbora is another genus of fish. parva: Latin, means "small".
